messages:
Aisha Malik: Heads-up — OrbitBank POC kickoff. They want SSE streaming (server-sent), function/tool calling, and strict structured JSON outputs for downstream systems. Also asked for a pricing ballpark for ~500 qps sustained and private/VPC options. Any immediate red flags or blockers?

Tom Bennett: Sounds doable. Main things to confirm: auth (short-lived creds vs. API key), IP allowlist for sockets, and whether they need KMS/HSM for keys. For SSE handshake we usually do:

Tom Bennett: ```http
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_token>
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Client-Id: orbitbank-poc
```

Tom Bennett: Server responds with 200 + event-stream and then sends JSON chunks. We can do function calls inline as structured messages — example payloads in docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/streaming/function-calls

Sasha Li: Security checklist: OrbitBank requires SOC2 + customer-managed KMS + IP allowlist + SAML SSO for console. For POC they'll accept SOC2 in our environment but want the KMS plan for Private. I'll own the questionnaire. @Aisha can you push the vendor form? :memo:

Ben Ortiz: Pricing note: for 500 qps sustained with streaming + tool calls, two levers matter: reserved GPU capacity (Dedicated) and egress/throughput tokens. Ballpark for committed Dedicated pool to meet latency SLOs is in the range of ~$18k–28k/mo depending on model size and quantization. If they want Private (VPC/on‑prem) add one-time infra + support overlay. I'll draft a short pricing note.

Aisha Malik: Thanks. Also they asked about SDKs for streaming — can we confirm Go + Rust support?

Tom Bennett: Yes — we have official Go SDK streaming examples, Rust has community SDK + examples. For presales POC we can give the Go example and a lightweight curl/SSE approach for Rust engineers. Example Go snippet:```go
client := redwood.NewClient("$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
stream, _ := client.Stream("gpt-stream", opts)
for msg := range stream.Recv() {
  fmt.Println(msg.Data)
}
```

Sasha Li: OrbitBank also flagged token rotation — recommend ephemeral tokens (STS) for the long run. For POC we can use short-lived API keys (1h) and show rotation flow.

Ben Ortiz: One technical caveat: function/tool calls that invoke external webhooks can increase tail latency. Recommend they run tool executions async or use our callback webhook with retry/backoff. We'll add a runbook snippet.

deploy-bot: Canary for presales-runbook-doc started by Tom Bennett at 2345679075

Tom Bennett: Runbook snippet to include in handoff: 1) Handshake example 2) Ephemeral token rotation flow 3) IP allowlist instructions 4) KMS integration notes 5) Observability dashboard links (latency/cost)

Aisha Malik: Action items: Sasha — fill vendor security form (owns). Tom — send runbook + Go examples (owns). Ben — draft price range + Dedicated sizing proposal (owns). I'll coordinate OrbitBank follow-up and schedule technical call.

Sasha Li: On it. Will upload the completed vendor form by EOD tomorrow.

Ben Ortiz: Drafting pricing now, will post a concise PDF in this thread by EOD.

Aisha Malik: Great — ping me if OrbitBank asks for an on‑prem checklist. Thanks all :thumbsup:
